Ronald Reagan's inauguration. On January 20, 1981, Ronald Reagan took the oath at age 69, becoming the oldest president inaugurated at that time. His inaugural address marked a decisive political realignment toward conservatism and anti-communist assertiveness. Government is not the solution to our problem, he declared; government is the problem. This statement captured his commitment to deregulation and reduced federal spending and would define his presidency and the rightward shift of American politics. He emphasized American economic and military strength as antidotes to Soviet communism. Reagan spoke directly to Soviet leaders in ideological terms, rejecting detente and calling for renewed American resolve. He promised a new beginning in American domestic and foreign policy, departing sharply from the Carter years. His inaugural parade cost over 16 million dollars, the most expensive to that date, reflecting his popularity among conservative Americans. Reagan's address set the stage for his presidency's defining themes: tax cuts, military buildup, and anti-communist interventionism abroad. He positioned the United States as locked in ideological struggle with the Soviet Union, rejecting the previous era's emphasis on arms control and diplomatic negotiation in favor of confrontation and American military superiority.
